title: Wombats poop tiny cubes!
question: Did you know a wombat's poop is shaped like little cubes?
answer: Wombats are the only known mammals whose poop comes out in the shape of little cubes.

visual.what: A cute wombat in a green Australian forest looks at the camera, with a pile of small brown cubes beside it and big sparkle marks around them.

parts.text: Did you know a wombat's poop is shaped like little cubes?

visual.what: Left side shows a dice-like cube with six square faces highlighted. Right side shows a small brown cube of wombat poop. An equals sign sits between them.

parts.text: Yes! A cube has six flat, square sides.

parts.text: A wombat is a furry animal from Australia, about one metre long. At night it eats grass, roots and plants.

parts.text: Poop is leftover food. In the large intestine, the body takes water out of it.

parts.text: Wombats are the only animals we know of whose poop is shaped like cubes. Scientists are still working out exactly how they make them.

facts.claim: Wombats are the only known mammals that excrete feces in a cubic shape.
Cubic feces let people know wombat habitats are nearby and show what the wombat may have eaten.
Wombats live in Australia, are about a metre long, are nocturnal and eat plants, roots and grasses.
Feces are the body's solid waste left over from eating food.
The large intestine takes water out of waste material before it leaves the body.
A cube has six square faces of the same size.

description: Wombats are the only known mammals that make cube-shaped poop! Find out what a cube is, what wombats eat, and why those little cubes are useful.
